See also: Prado

Galician

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese prado, from Latin prātum. Compare Portuguese and Spanish prado and English prairie.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpɾado/ [ˈpɾa.ð̞ʊ]
  • Rhymes: -ado
  • Hyphenation: Pra‧do

Noun

[edit]

prado m (plural prados)

  1. meadow; pasture
    Synonyms: lama, poulo, pradaría, pradeira, panasco, lamela, camposa, campío, anello, trulleiro, batuqueiro

Derived terms

[edit]
  • pradeira
  • Prado
  • Prado Vello
  • Pradolongo
  • Prados
  • Praducelo
  • Praducelos

References

[edit]
  • Seoane, Ernesto Xosé González; Granja, María Álvarez de la; Agrelo, Ana Isabel Boullón (2006–2022), “prado”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios do galego medieval [Dictionary of dictionaries of Medieval Galician] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Barreiro, Xavier Varela; Guinovart, Xavier Gómez (2006–2018), “prado”, in Corpus Xelmírez: corpus lingüístico da Galicia medieval [Corpus Xelmírez: linguistic corpus of Medieval Galicia] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, editor (2006–2013), “prado”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios da lingua galega [Dictionary of Dictionaries of the Galician language] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, Ernesto Xosé González Seoane, María Álvarez de la Granja, editors (2003–2018), “prado”, in Tesouro informatizado da lingua galega (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Rosario Álvarez Blanco, editor (2014–2024), “prado”, in Tesouro do léxico patrimonial galego e portugués (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega, →ISSN

Old Galician-Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin prātum.

Noun

[edit]

prado m (plural prados)

  1. meadow (an extensive area of grassland)

Descendants

[edit]
  • Galician: prado
  • Portuguese: prado

Further reading

[edit]
  • Universo Cantigas - "prado"

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese prado, Latin prātum. Compare Galician and Spanish prado and English prairie.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈpɾa.du/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈpɾa.du/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈpɾa.do/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈpɾa.du/ [ˈpɾa.ðu]

  • Audio (Brazil (Caipira)):(file)
  • Rhymes: (most dialects) -adu, (Southern Brazil) -ado
  • Hyphenation: pra‧do

Noun

[edit]

prado m (plural prados)

  1. meadow (an extensive area of grassland)
    Synonyms: pradaria, campina

Further reading

[edit]
  • “prado”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “prado”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Spanish

[edit]
Spanish Wikipedia has an article on:
prado
Wikipedia es

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin prātum. Related with English prairie.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpɾado/ [ˈpɾa.ð̞o]
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ado
  • Syllabification: pra‧do

Noun

[edit]

prado m (plural prados)

  1. meadow
    Synonyms: pradera, dehesa

Derived terms

[edit]
  • berro de prado
  • mastuerzo de prado
  • reina de los prados
  • trébol de prado

Related terms

[edit]
  • pradera

See also

[edit]
  • campo
  • campiña

Further reading

[edit]
  • “prado”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025

Anagrams

[edit]
  • pardo, podar, podrá
